entry.title: More than one language in family life
entry.summary: The authors describe familiar people, places and routines as ways a baby can meet more than one language. Their examples offer different arrangements for different families.
entry.cue: More than one language is part of your baby’s family or community.
detail: One example gives each caregiver a language to use with the baby. Another connects languages with particular places or times, such as home, outings or weekends.
Books, play and conversation with people who speak a language are further possibilities. These arrangements need to fit the people and resources a family has.

references.locator: Opening paragraph: principles adapted to individual families

ageContext.bookAge: Infancy discussion; no fixed starting or finishing month for the family arrangements.
ageContext.readiness: More than one language belongs to the family’s people, places or routines.
ageContext.note: The activity may continue while it fits your child’s interest and current skills; the source ages are guides.

displayContext.footer: You don’t need a different home. Start with what you have.
displayContext.colophon: Original summaries inspired by The Montessori Baby and The Montessori Toddler. Open any idea for its book references. The illustration is an invitation to explore, rather than a room to reproduce. Follow your child’s pace.
